When NATO was founded in 1949, it was controversial both in the US and in Europe, but at least at that time there was a plausible justification for it. At the time, the American commitment to NATO was presented as temporary: NATO Supreme Commander Dwight Eisenhower said, “If in ten years, all American troops stationed in Europe for national defense purposes have not been returned to the United States, then this whole project will have failed.”

NATO should have been dissolved in the sixties, once the European nations had rebuilt their economies and were again capable of providing for their own defense. After the collapse of the Communist bloc in 1989, the argument in favor of NATO lost the last shred of credibility.
